title: Read a JSON file
description: Load a UTF-8 JSON file into Python dictionaries and lists.
code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("data.json")
with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as file:
    data = json.load(file)

title: Convert JSON to a pandas DataFrame
description: Read a JSON file containing a list of records into a pandas DataFrame. For nested records, use the flatten snippet.
code:
import json
import pandas as pd

# Expected JSON: [{"name": "Ada", "score": 95}]
with open("data.json", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    records = json.load(file)

df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

title: Write a dictionary to JSON
description: Save a dictionary as readable UTF-8 JSON with indentation.
code:
import json

data = {"name": "Ada", "score": 95}
with open("output.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    json.dump(data, file, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

title: Parse a JSON string
description: Convert JSON text already in memory into a Python object.
code:
import json

text = '{"name": "Ada", "active": true}'
data = json.loads(text)

title: Read CSV into a pandas DataFrame
description: Load a comma-separated file with a header row into pandas.
code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv", encoding="utf-8")

title: Flatten nested JSON with pandas
description: Turn nested dictionaries in JSON records into flat, dotted DataFrame columns.
code:
import pandas as pd

records = [{"name": "Ada", "address": {"city": "London"}}]
df = pd.json_normalize(records, sep=".")
# Columns: name, address.city

title: Remove duplicates from a list
description: Keep the first occurrence of each hashable item, preserving its original order.
code:
items = ["apple", "pear", "apple", "orange"]
unique_items = list(dict.fromkeys(items))
# ['apple', 'pear', 'orange']; items must be hashable.

title: Sort a list of dictionaries by a key
description: Return records ordered by one dictionary field without changing the input list.
code:
records = [{"name": "Ada", "score": 95}, {"name": "Lin", "score": 88}]
sorted_records = sorted(records, key=lambda record: record["score"])
# Add reverse=True for descending order.

title: List files in a directory
description: Find regular files directly inside a folder with pathlib; does not recurse into subfolders.
code:
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path(".")
files = sorted(path for path in folder.iterdir() if path.is_file())
for path in files:
    print(path.name)

title: Convert a date string to datetime
description: Parse a date in a known format into a naive datetime object.
code:
from datetime import datetime

text = "2026-09-12"
date = datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d")
